newsitem.title: KENYA: Corporate bond trading launched on Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Corporate bond trading launched on Nairobi bourse.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange launched trade in corporate bonds on Tuesday in what major players hailed as testament to the improved business environment since the government launched economic reforms in earnest three years ago.
Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) chairman Jimnah Mbaru said the introduction of corporate bonds in the secondary market was "very timely and useful".
He added: "But in order to make bonds more attractive to investors I would like to call upon the government to suspend withholding tax on corporate bonds for the next five years."
But Jimnah Mbaru also said that changes in the financial sector had created a big challenge to companies because the availability of cheap funds was not there.
"The major problem for companies and the economy in general is the prevailing high interest rates," Mbaru said in a speech.
"The effective lending rate is about 30 percent in a low inflationary environment. With the annual inflation at 8.7 percent, the real interest rate is above 20 percent," Mbaru said.

"This discourages investments and makes economic growth more elusive," Mbaru said. He added that for Kenya's economy to grow at a rate of 7.0 percent annually to eradicate poverty and unemployment, the challenge lay squarely in the monetary authorities devising strategies to make credit affordable.
Kenya's economy is forecast to grow at 5.5 percent in 1996.
The first batch of bonds on the NSE were issued by the East African Bank and were worth 600 million shillings ($10.8 million). They made their debut on the secondary market on December 9.
Bonds are the third tradeable instrument on the bourse after equity, preference shares and loan stocks.
The bonds are due in 1999 and are denominated in a million shillings. Interest will be payable quarterly in arrears on February 22, May 22, August 22 and November 22 in each year.
East African Development Bank is a multilateral development bank whose members are the governments Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda and nine financial institutions.

A separate bonds board has been set up at the NSE. For a deal to take place, the buyers bid must match the sellers offer. The applicable reference interest rate will be the prevailing rate of the day on the 91-day treasury bill rate plus 1.2 percent.
